reason: E2 supports the role of high mixing entropy in stabilizing solid-solution phases at high temperatures, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that lattice distortion suppresses atomic diffusion or that this mechanism governs stability against phase segregation in HEA nanoparticles. The key mechanistic premises linking lattice distortion to diffusion and stability are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: High mixing entropy stabilizes single-phase solid solutions in HEAs at high temperatures.
Lattice distortion (from atomic size mismatch) suppresses atomic diffusion.
Suppressed diffusion counteracts phase segregation or chemical ordering.
HEA nanoparticles with lower lattice distortion are more prone to diffusion-driven phase separation.
